author: Robert Carr
description: Cumin-coriander roasted cauliflower and chickpeas with farro, lemon-softened kale, green herb-tahini sauce, dates, almonds and pomegranate. A filling plant-based meal with toasted spices, citrus and contrasting textures; no tofu.
equipment: Five shallow meal-prep containers and separate sauce/topping cups

groceryIngredients.note: Unseasoned 10-12-minute pearled variety, not a long-cooking whole farro.
3 g total; use a fine salt weighing about 6 g per teaspoon.
15 oz each; approximately 500 g drained and rinsed total.
Ready-trimmed florets keep prep within the stated time.
284 g trimmed leaves, without tough stems.
About 1 cup; purchase ready-to-eat arils for the stated timing.

ingredients: Farro: 150 g dry unseasoned quick-cooking farro, a 10-12-minute variety
Farro: 4 cups water for cooking and 1/8 teaspoon (0.75 g) fine sea salt for finishing after draining
Roast: two 15-oz cans no-salt-added chickpeas, drained, rinsed and dried, approximately 500 g drained total
Roast: 2 lb (907 g) cauliflower florets, cut into 1-inch pieces
Roast: 1 large red onion (225 g peeled), cut into 1/2-inch wedges
Roast: 2 teaspoons ground cumin, 2 teaspoons ground coriander and 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
Roast: 1/2 teaspoon ground turmeric, 1/4 teaspoon cayenne and 1/4 teaspoon (1.5 g) fine sea salt
Greens: 10 oz (284 g) trimmed kale leaves, thinly sliced, and 2 tablespoons (30 mL) fresh lemon juice
Sauce: 1/4 cup (60 g) unsalted tahini, well stirred
Sauce: 3 tablespoons (45 g) fresh lemon juice and 1/4 cup (60 g) water
Sauce: 1 garlic clove (4 g peeled), finely grated, and 1/8 teaspoon (0.75 g) fine sea salt
Sauce: 1/2 cup (15 g) finely chopped flat-leaf parsley and 1/2 cup (15 g) finely chopped cilantro
Finish: 2 Medjool dates (48 g pitted flesh), finely chopped
Finish: 35 g chopped unsalted roasted almonds, about 1/4 cup
Finish: 175 g pomegranate arils, about 1 cup
Greens: 2 tablespoons (30 mL) water for briefly steaming the kale
instructions: Start the oven and farro: Heat the oven to 450 F with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Bring 4 cups water to a boil in a saucepan. Add 150 g quick-cooking farro and simmer for its package's 10-12-minute time, until chewy but tender. Drain thoroughly and toss with 1/8 teaspoon (0.75 g) fine sea salt. Do not use a long-cooking variety and expect the same elapsed time.

Season the roast: In the large mixing bowl, combine the drained chickpeas from two 15-oz cans (about 500 g drained), 2 lb (907 g) cauliflower florets and 225 g red onion wedges. Toss very thoroughly with 2 tablespoons olive oil, 2 teaspoons cumin, 2 teaspoons coriander, 1 teaspoon smoked paprika, 1/2 teaspoon turmeric, 1/4 teaspoon cayenne and 1/4 teaspoon (1.5 g) fine sea salt.

Roast without crowding: Spread the seasoned chickpea-cauliflower-onion mixture across both sheet pans in a single layer. Roast for 25-30 minutes, turning the vegetables and swapping the pans' rack positions after 15 minutes. Look for dark golden cauliflower edges and tender stems; the chickpeas should be lightly browned, not dried into hard snacks.

Make the green sauce while the vegetables roast: Whisk 1/4 cup (60 g) tahini, 3 tablespoons (45 g) lemon juice, 1/4 cup (60 g) water, 4 g grated garlic and 1/8 teaspoon (0.75 g) fine sea salt until smooth. Stir in 1/2 cup (15 g) chopped parsley and 1/2 cup (15 g) chopped cilantro. These measured ingredients make about 200 g sauce. Refrigerate until portioning.

Soften the kale: In the cleaned 6-quart mixing bowl, toss 10 oz (284 g) thinly sliced kale leaves with 2 tablespoons (30 mL) lemon juice and massage for 90 seconds. Transfer the massaged kale to the 3-quart saucepan with the cooked farro made from 150 g dry farro and 2 tablespoons (30 mL) water. Cover and steam over medium-low heat for 2-3 minutes, stirring once, until the kale is tender enough to eat comfortably. Return the kale and farro to the mixing bowl. This avoids relying on residual heat from farro that finished cooking much earlier.

Combine the hot components: Add the roasted mixture made from two cans chickpeas, 2 lb cauliflower and 225 g onion to the farro-kale bowl. Fold in 2 finely chopped Medjool dates (48 g pitted flesh), distributing the small pieces through the grains rather than leaving sticky clumps.

Portion: Weigh the finished grain-vegetable mixture and distribute it evenly among five shallow containers. Pack about 40 g green tahini sauce, 35 g pomegranate arils and 7 g chopped almonds for each meal in separate cups. Keep sauce and pomegranate refrigerated, and keep the almonds dry. Add these toppings after reheating rather than microwaving them with the vegetables.
notes: Timing: About 55 minutes including oven preheating, preparation and portioning, using ready-trimmed cauliflower, prepared pomegranate arils and 10-12-minute farro. Two full-size sheet pans are required for browning; crowding this volume onto one pan steams the vegetables.

Meal prep: Refrigerate shallow portions, the green sauce and pomegranate at 40 F or colder within 2 hours of preparation, or 1 hour above 90 F. Use within 3-4 days. Keep almonds separate so they stay crunchy. Chickpeas soften during storage; the separately packed nuts provide the reliable reheated-meal crunch.

Five portions, not five fridge days: Eat two portions on one day, or freeze the extra hot-component portion on prep day. Freeze any portion that will not be eaten within 3-4 days. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator and reheat the next day. Sauce and pomegranate are best within their refrigerated window; freezing can change their texture.

Reheating: Add 1 tablespoon water to one grain-vegetable portion, cover with a vented lid and heat in short microwave intervals, stirring between intervals, until it reaches 165 F in several places. Add that meal's 40 g green tahini sauce, 35 g pomegranate and 7 g almonds after heating.

Portion options: The base makes five generous vegetable-forward meals. For more energy, divide the same batch into four meals and use about 50 g sauce, 44 g pomegranate and 8.75 g almonds per meal. For additional protein without tofu, add 170 g plain nonfat Greek yogurt to an individual meal as a separate savory side; this changes the vegan and milk-allergen status and is not included in base nutrition.

Health-conscious review: Chickpeas, vegetables, seeds and nuts provide fiber and plant protein with measured olive oil and salt. Quick-cooking pearled farro is not necessarily a whole grain; the label is based on the complete meal, not an unsupported whole-grain claim. Portions and the rest of the day's intake determine suitability for weight loss or bulking.

Food-safety basis: USDA Leftovers and Food Safety, https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/leftovers-and-food-safety. Eating-pattern basis: NIH DASH, https://www.nhlbi.nih.gov/health/dash-eating-plan.
Allergens: Wheat, sesame and almonds. Original recipe developed for this collection; not kitchen-tested.
